about_html:
Kmetija Moro is a family farm at Vipolže 62 in Goriška Brda, Slovenia, near the Italian border. It sells its wines as Moro Wines. According to the family, the farm goes back to the great-grandmother Margerita; the name comes from a grandfather nicknamed Moro because of his black hair. The family cultivates 7 hectares of vineyards and 5 hectares of orchards. The Jakončič family runs it: Boris and Dragica Jakončič and Damjan Jakončič, the junior head.

Since 2018 the Kulturinitiative bewegungINkultur from Klagenfurt has organised the exhibition series “Kunst in den Hügeln – Umetnost v Brdih – Arte nel Collio” in the farm’s hall, with artists from Carinthia, Friuli and Slovenia. The organisers call the place the “Kunstbotschaft Kärntens in Slowenien” (Slovenian “Ambasada umetnosti Koroške v Sloveniji”, Italian “Ambasciata d’arte della Carinzia in Slovenia”). In 2026 the exhibitions changed in spring and autumn. Visits are by telephone appointment.

Séverin Krön was born in 1964 in Nanterre near Paris and grew up bilingual. From 1985 to 1992 he studied painting and art education in Vienna and at the Mozarteum in Salzburg; his teachers included Arnulf Rainer and Anton Lehmden. Since 2007 he has made “Art permutable”: pictures of square panels that can be moved and turned. Myths are a frequent subject, as in a series on the Ring of the Nibelung from 2014. He has had solo exhibitions in Vienna, Paris, Linz, Salzburg, Corbeil and Bern, worked in the International Guest Studio Maltator in Gmünd in 2015 and showed his work at the KUNSTradln gallery in Millstatt in 2019. In January 2022 he followed Elisabeth Kleinwächter as head of the Galerie im Schloss Porcia in Spittal an der Drau, where he curates the exhibitions.

about_html:
Gerhard Lepicnik has family roots in Sittersdorf (Žitara vas) and lives in Klagenfurt. He is a graduate engineer (Dipl.-Ing.) and worked for the Carinthian electricity company KELAG, where he was an authorised officer and co-wrote the chapter on grid construction in a company history. He retired as head of the former Netzleitung Ost (eastern grid control) in St. Veit. In 2020 he completed a Master of Arts in Applied Cultural Studies at the University of Klagenfurt with a thesis on Pier Paolo Pasolini and Friulian poetry.

From 1970 he chaired the choir Sängerrunde Ebenthal. In 1972 he and the choir leader Heinz Fischer invited the Slovenian choir from Radsberg to a concert in Ebenthal, and the audience boycotted the Sängerrunde in return (source: Thomas Ogris, Kärnten Dokumentation, vol. 38, 2023). According to Tomaž Ogris, the encounters “Dober večer, sosed” (Good evening, neighbour) could not have been realised without him and Hans Mosser (source: novice.at, 2021). On 26 June 2009 the City of Klagenfurt awarded him its Ehrpfennig for his cultural work, especially as long-time chairman of the Singkreis Seltenheim.

He has presented artists from Friuli in Carinthia since 2013 at the latest. He is the main organiser of the Kulturinitiative bewegungINkultur, which shows exhibitions with artists from Carinthia, Friuli and Slovenia, among them the Trigeniale in the Studiogalerie of the Klagenfurt Stadthaus. In 2018 he and the winegrower Boris Jakončič started the exhibition series “Kunst in den Hügeln – Umetnost v Brdih” at the Kmetija Moro in Vipolže, Goriška Brda. In 2024 ORF reported that he had organised about twelve exhibitions with some 30 artists in the previous six years. As a student of the University of Klagenfurt he took part in the art projects “BAUM | MENSCH | KLANG | KUNST” (2014) and “For Forest” (2019) and in the Slavic studies exhibition “Landschaft & Identität” (2023). He is married to the artist Marlis Lepicnik.

Gerhard Lepicnik hat familiäre Wurzeln in Sittersdorf (Žitara vas) und lebt in Klagenfurt. Er ist Diplomingenieur und arbeitete für die Kärntner Elektrizitäts-AG (KELAG), wo er Handlungsbevollmächtigter war und in einer Firmengeschichte das Kapitel „Netzbau“ mitverfasste. Er ging als Leiter der ehemaligen Netzleitung Ost in St. Veit in Pension. 2020 schloss er an der Universität Klagenfurt das Masterstudium Angewandte Kulturwissenschaft mit einer Arbeit über Pier Paolo Pasolini und die friulanische Lyrik ab (Master of Arts).

Ab 1970 war er Obmann der Sängerrunde Ebenthal. Als er 1972 mit dem Chorleiter Heinz Fischer den slowenischen Chor aus Radsberg zu einem Konzert in Ebenthal einlud, wurde die Sängerrunde mit einem Boykott des Publikums bestraft (Quelle: Thomas Ogris, Kärnten Dokumentation, Band 38, 2023). Juni 2009 erhielt er für seine Verdienste um die Kultur, besonders als langjähriger Obmann des Singkreises Seltenheim, den Ehrpfennig der Landeshauptstadt Klagenfurt.

Spätestens seit 2013 präsentiert er Kunstschaffende aus Friaul in Kärnten. Er ist Hauptorganisator der Kulturinitiative bewegungINkultur, die Ausstellungen mit Kunstschaffenden aus Kärnten, Friaul und Slowenien zeigt, darunter die Trigeniale in der Studiogalerie des Klagenfurter Stadthauses. 2018 begann er mit dem Weinbauern Boris Jakončič die Ausstellungsreihe „Kunst in den Hügeln – Umetnost v Brdih“ in der Kmetija Moro in Vipolže, Goriška Brda. 2024 berichtete der ORF, dass er in den vorangegangenen sechs Jahren rund zwölf Ausstellungen mit etwa 30 Kunstschaffenden organisiert hatte. Als Student der Universität Klagenfurt wirkte er an den Kunstprojekten „BAUM | MENSCH | KLANG | KUNST“ (2014) und „For Forest“ (2019) sowie an der Ausstellung „Landschaft & Identität“ der Slawistik (2023) mit. Burgis Paier was born in Klagenfurt in 1949 and died there in 2022. She worked as a costume and stage designer and as a visual artist: figures, objects, automata, collages, reliquaries, rooms, puppets and embroidery. From 1977 she showed her work in solo exhibitions in Udine, Milan, Bologna, Klagenfurt, Vienna, Graz, Linz and Salzburg, among other places, several of them together with Günter Brus, such as “Kaspar Hauser” (2008) and the two “Phantasus” exhibitions (2010, 2011). In 2017 she was artist in residence at the Red Gate Residency in Beijing. Her last cycle, Das große Welttheater, was shown in 2020 in the Alpen-Adria-Galerie in Klagenfurt and has been the permanent exhibition of the Theatergalerie since December 2022.

Theres Cassini was born in Rattendorf in the Gail Valley, Carinthia, in 1960 and lives and works in Vienna. She trained in mechanical engineering and industrial technology at a technical college in Vienna and attended acting school; from 1988 to 1993 she made textile object art under the name CASSINI + MARLOWE. After an apprenticeship in his parents’ painting business he studied at the art school in Linz under Herbert Dimmel from 1953 to 1957, at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna under Herbert Boeckl from 1957 to 1961 and at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris in 1963/64. In 1965 he settled in Krumpendorf am Wörthersee, where he still lives and works. His paintings start from landscape motifs and reduce them to a few areas of colour close to abstraction.

He lives and works in Vienna and, since 2002, in St. Veit im Jauntal.

In 2018, when a serious illness first confronted her with her own mortality, the Klagenfurt costume designer and artist Burgis Paier began to stage her great world theatre: 350 figures of people from art and cultural history who had shaped her life and work – artists, writers, composers, philosophers, singers, fashion designers, actors, freedom fighters, explorers, scientists and even fairy-tale characters. They are neither puppets nor classical sculptures but hybrids of the two, and every figure has the artist’s hands. First shown in 2020 in the Alpen-Adria-Galerie, the cycle has been the permanent exhibition of the Theatergalerie since it opened in December 2022. Presentations on the theme of theatre change every half year and enter into dialogue with it.

2018, als eine schwere Krankheit sie zum ersten Mal mit ihrer eigenen Sterblichkeit konfrontierte, begann die Klagenfurter Kostümbildnerin und Künstlerin Burgis Paier, ihr großes Welttheater zu inszenieren: 350 Figuren von Persönlichkeiten der Kunst- und Kulturgeschichte, die für ihr Leben und ihre Kunst prägend waren – Künstler:innen, Schriftsteller:innen, Komponist:innen, Philosoph:innen, Sänger:innen, Modeschöpfer:innen, Schauspieler:innen, Freiheitskämpfer:innen, Entdecker:innen, Naturwissenschafter:innen und sogar Märchenfiguren. description:
Eighty years after the end of the Second World War, the Museum der Stadt Villach shows how wars end, in German and English. Six conflicts, from the Napoleonic Wars to the war in Ukraine, are linked to the history of Villach. Eleven eyewitnesses tell of flight, violence and new beginnings. Among the objects are a defused aerial bomb from the Second World War, a replica of an alpine position from the First World War and a Lada from Ukraine that was shot at by both sides. For 2026 the exhibition was extended and updated, with new content on the Cold War, the war in Ukraine and the sinking of the warship “Szent István”. It ends in a Peace Lab with interactive stations; two of them were developed by pupils of the BG/BRG Villach St. Martin.

The 18th exhibition of the series “Kunst in den Hügeln – Umetnost v Brdih – Arte nel Collio” shows paintings by three women artists from Friuli, Slovenia and Carinthia in the hall of the Kmetija Moro winery in Vipolže, Goriška Brda. Giulia Cernetig (Udine) belongs to the Gruppo artistico culturale Albrecht Dürer in Tavagnacco. Aleksandra Rusjan (Brda), a member of the artists’ association DABLO, shows among other works “Kanjon”, “Češnja” and Dobrovo Castle. Margrit Pernull (Hermagor) shows landscapes of the Nockberge and the Weissensee, fruit and flowers. The Kulturinitiative bewegungINkultur organises the exhibition with both associations, under the patronage of the Alpe-Adria Center for Cross-border Cooperation (AACC). Franc Mužič, mayor of Brda, opened it; it was his last opening in the series, as he leaves office in November 2026.

The Stadttheater Klagenfurt was built from 1908 to 1910 to designs by the Viennese firm Fellner & Helmer as the Kaiser-Franz-Joseph-Jubiläumstheater, for the 60th jubilee of Emperor Franz Joseph I. It was renovated in the 1960s and again from 1996 to 1998 to designs by Günther Domenig, and it received Nestroy Theatre Prizes in 2003, 2006 and 2011. Its artistic director (Intendant) is Aron Stiehl. Since 2011 the theatre has staged the works of Richard Wagner with marked intensity, from Der fliegende Holländer (2011) to Tristan und Isolde (2025).

The works by members of the association circled around opposites, encounters and shifting points of view – the contrasts that arise where different things meet. The range of motifs, techniques and approaches was correspondingly wide, from gestural painting to drawing. The announcement named Siegfried Zellot, Gudrun Zikulnig, Slava Mohl, Alfred Scheikl and Sylvia Campidell. Guided tours started at 18:00, and the artists were present for conversation. The association from Velden am Wörther See has taken part in the Lange Nacht with themed exhibitions since 2004. PERMAPHEMERA recorded the exhibition as a 360° tour, which is being prepared for publication here.

Sources

  • langenacht.orf.at
  • kunstverein-velden.at

Der Kunstverein Velden zeigte zur ORF-Langen Nacht der Museen 2026 im großen und kleinen Saal im ersten Stock des Klagenfurter Europahauses die Gemeinschaftsausstellung „Spannungsfelder und Perspektiven“. Die Arbeiten von Vereinsmitgliedern kreisten um Gegensätze, Begegnungen und wechselnde Blickwinkel – um jene Kontraste, die entstehen, wo Unterschiedliches aufeinandertrifft. Entsprechend breit war das Spektrum an Motiven, Techniken und Zugängen, von gestischer Malerei bis zur Zeichnung. Angekündigt waren Siegfried Zellot, Gudrun Zikulnig, Slava Mohl, Alfred Scheikl und Sylvia Campidell. Ab 18 Uhr fanden Führungen statt, die anwesenden Künstlerinnen und Künstler standen für Gespräche bereit. Der Verein aus Velden am Wörther See beteiligt sich seit 2004 regelmäßig mit Themenausstellungen an der Langen Nacht. PERMAPHEMERA hat die Ausstellung als 360°-Tour aufgenommen; sie wird für die Veröffentlichung hier vorbereitet.

about_html:
Karl Nackler grew up in Upper Carinthia and lives in Klagenfurt. During his working life as a manager of a Carinthian energy company he already drew and painted. He took courses in caricature with Wilfried Steurer and in nude and portrait drawing with Ulrike Reinwald, and repeatedly attended the art forum “Zeitlos” of Herbert Schwei. He now concentrates on drawings in white chalk on black card: portraits of conductors, architects, writers and other public figures, nudes and the hands of old people. In still lifes and pictures of insects and flowers he adds colour with pastel.

He has exhibited at the Pädagogisches Institut in Klagenfurt, in a group exhibition in Cologne, at the Europahaus Klagenfurt (portraits of the founding fathers of the EU), at the Galerie Kreativraum in Vienna (“Liebe auf den ersten Blick”) and in Friuli and Slovenia.

about_html:
Herbert Boeckl was born in Klagenfurt on 3 June 1894 and died in Vienna on 20 January 1966. After an unsuccessful application to the Vienna Academy of Fine Arts, he studied architecture at the Technische Hochschule in Vienna from 1912 and took private lessons with Adolf Loos. From 1935 he was a professor at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna. He joined the NSDAP in 1941 and was classified as “politically unreliable” in 1944; in 1945 he became provisional rector of the Academy and in 1946 he was removed from that office because he had not registered as a former NSDAP member in 1945 (source: Belvedere chronology, belvedere.at/herbert-boeckl). From 1951 to 1960 he painted the frescoes of the Angel Chapel in Seckau Abbey, and in 1962 the Academy elected him rector. Since 2011 the Stadttheater Klagenfurt has staged Richard Wagner with marked intensity, from Der fliegende Holländer to Tristan und Isolde. The Theatergalerie shows four costumes from Wagner’s Walküre and Tristan und Isolde together with their designs, and turns to the work behind the curtain: the theatre’s tailoring and make-up departments, headed by Bettina Breitenecker and Renate Wutte. Stage photographs by Arnold Pöschl accompany the costumes. Curated by Günter Schmidauer, in cooperation with the Stadttheater Klagenfurt, which lent the works. The room also holds Burgis Paier’s permanent installation Das große Welttheater.

She trained at the State College of Architecture and Construction in Minsk and studied graphics and printmaking at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, graduating in 2023. Karlheinz Simonitsch was born in Lienz, East Tyrol, in 1953, went to school in Klagenfurt, where Egon Wucherer was one of his teachers, and graduated from the University of Graz. He taught at the Handelsakademie Klagenfurt until 2003 and worked as a freelance artist with a studio in Klagenfurt; in 1995 he worked at the City of Klagenfurt's studio in Šmartno. From the 1990s he turned increasingly to sacred subjects and church interiors, working in drawing, watercolour, oil and mixed media as well as in glass and ceramics, for example the glass cross “Ich bin das Leben” (1998) in the parish church of Klagenfurt-Wölfnitz. He died in December 2015.

Franz Grabmayr was born in Obervellach, Carinthia, in 1927 and died in Vienna in 2015. He first worked as a teacher, studied at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna in the afternoons from 1954 and gave up teaching in 1964 to work only as an artist. He lived and painted in the northern Waldviertel, first at Schloss Rosenau and later on a farm near Zwettl, and spent the winters in a studio in the Karl-Marx-Hof in Vienna. His pictures are built up from very thick layers of paint; his subjects include fire, sand pits, mountain streams and dancers.

She announced it as a contribution to the Triennale IV Kärnten and its theme “schwach.šibko.debole”. The exhibition set cracks, breaks and frayed edges against the ideal of smooth, flawless surfaces and read them as traces of movement, time and resistance: imperfection not as a lack but as a form of honesty. Urach studied at the Freie Akademie der Bildenden Künste in Klagenfurt; she works abstractly and combines painting with paper and collaged elements. The artist was present for talks and guided tours from 18:00. PERMAPHEMERA recorded the exhibition as a 360° tour, which is being prepared for publication here.

The Kulturinitiative bewegung / movimento / gibanje IN kultur (short: bewegungINkultur) is based in Klagenfurt and names itself in German, Italian and Slovenian. Since 2015 it has kept up friendly and cultural contacts with artists and organisations in Friuli and Slovenia, above all with the Gruppo artistico culturale Albrecht Dürer in Tavagnacco near Udine, the artists' association DABLO in Goriška Brda and the Circolo Culturale ENDAS in Monfalcone. With them it organises bilateral and trilateral exhibitions in Carinthia, Friuli and the Slovenian Littoral.

In Klagenfurt the initiative shows its three-country exhibitions in the Studiogalerie of the Stadthaus, since 2024 under the title Trigeniale. Since 2018 it has run the exhibition series “Kunst in den Hügeln – Umetnost v Brdih – Arte nel Collio” at the Kmetija Moro winery in Vipolže, Goriška Brda, where artists from Carinthia exhibit. It also organises cultural trips to castles, palaces and exhibitions in Friuli and Slovenia. Its contact person and main organiser is Gerhard Lepicnik.

With them it organises bilateral and trilateral exhibitions in Carinthia, Friuli and the Slovenian Littoral.

In Klagenfurt the initiative shows its three-country exhibitions in the Studiogalerie of the Stadthaus, since 2024 under the title Trigeniale. Since 2018 it has run the exhibition series “Kunst in den Hügeln – Umetnost v Brdih – Arte nel Collio” at the Kmetija Moro winery in Vipolže, Goriška Brda, where artists from Carinthia exhibit. It also organises cultural trips to castles, palaces and exhibitions in Friuli and Slovenia. Its contact person and main organiser is Gerhard Lepicnik.
